title: Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| $\geq 1$ in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene
authors: Qiu Yang, Zihao Huo, Le Liu, Tianqi Song, Fankun Wang, Jingwei Dong, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Weibo Gao, Xiaobo Lu, Guangyu Zhang, Wei Yang
abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Here, we observe a coexistence of superconductivity and Chern insulators in a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moiré superlattice. Superconductivity, evidenced by a sharp transition with a critical temperature of ~180 mK, nonlinear I-V with a BKT temperature of 135 mK, and a signature of phase-sensitive interference patterns, emerges from a symmetry-breaking Fermi surface near v = -2 and D = 0, and it survives at a large in-plane magnetic field up to 2 T, strongly deviating from the Pauli limit. Moreover, we observe a strong modulation of the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length from 467 nm to 145 nm as the in-plane magnetic field increases from 0 to 2 T, whereas the critical current Ic barely changes. Unlike previous studies in RMG, we observe a competition between superconductivity and a correlated insulator at v = -2, monitored by displacement fields and twist angles. Note that we also observe integer Chern insulators with C = 1, 3, and -3 at v = 1/2, 1, and 3, respectively, for large D > 0 in the same superconducting device. The observations establish twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers as a fascinating system to investigate unconventional superconductivity, high Chern number topology, and their interplay.
summary: This work reports the observation of superconductivity coexisting with high-Chern-number Chern insulators in twisted rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices. By using low-temperature transport measurements, the authors map out the phase diagram, demonstrating that the system can host both unconventional superconductivity and robust topological insulating states simultaneously. This establishes the material as a tunable platform for studying the interplay between superconductivity and topology.
main_problem: The study investigates the coexistence and competition between superconductivity and topological phases, specifically Chern insulators, in a moiré superlattice system.
main_result: The authors successfully observed the coexistence of superconductivity (with $T_c \approx 180$ mK) and integer Chern insulators ($C=\pm 1, 3$) in twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers.
method: The research employed low-temperature transport measurements, including nonlinear I-V curves, quantum oscillation analysis (Landau fan), and Ginzburg-Landau fitting to characterize the superconducting and topological states.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moiré superlattice, whose electronic properties are tuned by gate voltages (displacement field $D$) and applied in-plane magnetic fields ($B_{//}$).
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), BKT transition temperature, Chern numbers ($C$), coherence length ($\xi_{GL}$), and quantized Hall conductance ($ho_{xy}$).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on continuum models and fitting the transport data to established theories like Ginzburg-Landau theory for coherence length.
figures_summary: Figures map out the phase diagrams showing SC pockets bordering correlated insulating regions, and Landau fan diagrams confirm quantized Hall plateaus corresponding to specific Chern numbers.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase space by varying filling factor and magnetic fields, first establishing SC signatures, then confirming CI states via quantization, and finally demonstrating the competition/coexistence between these two orders.
why_interesting: The interplay between unconventional superconductivity and topological order (Chern insulators) is a major frontier in condensed matter physics, providing a clean platform to study emergent quantum phenomena.
